Two more Mayflower men stand behind the Muirs, on DeWitt’s mother’s side.
George Sole came as a servant: Bradford lists “two men servants, called George Sole and Elias Story” in Edward Winslow’s
household. He signed the Compact all the same, and in time took land of his own at Duxbury.
In 1637 his name is among the “Voluntaries” for the Pequot War, and he sat for Duxbury in the colony’s court.
His will of 1677 thanks his eldest son John, who “hath in my extreme old age and weakness been tender and careful
of me”, then adds that if John should ever “disturb my daughter Patience” the gift is void.
Francis Eaton was a house carpenter, baptised at Saint Thomas’s in Bristol in 1596.
He brought his wife Sarah and a son Bradford remembered as “a sucking child”; Sarah died that winter.
